question: The up-or-down check on the running product is asked by monitoring equipment on a schedule, not by a person. Should that equipment be named as a role of its own, or is the check plumbing with nobody behind it?

candidates.description: Name the monitoring equipment as a role of its own, alongside the chat user and the person who set the product up.

payload.name: Deployment Monitor
payload.description:
Whatever watches the running product from outside and needs a quick answer on whether it is still up: a load balancer deciding where to send traffic, a container platform deciding whether to restart it, an uptime monitor deciding whether to page somebody.

It is equipment rather than a person, it asks on a fixed schedule rather than because anything happened, and it never takes part in a conversation. The only thing it asks for is the up-or-down check.

candidates.description: Leave the check with nobody behind it: it is plumbing for the deployment, not something anyone in the product does.

context: qry.serviceHealth (src/conciergent/app.py:149, tests/test_app.py:60) has no performedBy edge. The graph declares only two actors, actor.chatUser and actor.appBuilder, and neither fits: the node's own description says it is asked by "a load balancer, a container platform, an uptime monitor" on a fixed schedule. The DDD ontology allows an actor to be a system role, not only a person. This is the one operation in the graph whose issuer is genuinely external to the product yet unmodelled; the other 18 unwired operations are all issued internally by the product itself and their omission looks deliberate. Candidate A adds an actor node plus a performedBy edge from qry.serviceHealth; candidate B leaves the graph as it stands.
